entries.text: The relevant bronzeware inscription form shows a variant# of 尹 (harmonious circle) + 二 (align) → objects arranged in a neat circle → *equal*; *uniform* → (place in) *balance*; *even*.

A hybrid of 文 and the katakana メ. A 文 (もん) was a coin of slight value used in the Edo Period. メ suggests a Japanese term meaning "graduation." 匁 was devised to convey the meaning "a *measure of weight* equivalent to that of a 文 coin" → (approximately 3.75 grams).

勹 here suggesting a bent arm + a cursive rendering of 二 (align) → line objects in a neat circle. *Fragrance*, *perfume*, *scent* and *brilliantly colored* are extended meanings (← harmonious ← well-balanced ← neat circle) → *shine brilliantly* (← brilliantly colored).

The relevant seal inscription form shows a person using his hands to restrain another, cutting off the latter's progress → *entreat*; *beg*; *beggar* (← cut off another person's progress in order to entreat/beg) → *give* (← give to one who begs).
气也。逯安說：亡人爲匄。

translation.text: Breath or vapor. Lu An says: a fugitive is called 匄.

entries.text: A depiction of a placenta/womb that envelops a fetus → *envelop*; *wrap*.
象人褢妊，巳在中，象子未成形也。元气起於子。子，人所生也。男左行三十，女右行二十，俱立於巳，爲夫婦。褢妊於巳，巳爲子，十月而生。男起巳至寅，女起巳至申。故男秊始寅，女秊始申也。凡包之屬皆从包。

translation.text: Depicts a pregnant person, with 巳 inside representing a child not yet fully formed. Primal qi begins at 子; a child is what people produce. The male moves leftward for thirty, the female rightward for twenty; both stand at 巳 and become husband and wife. Pregnancy begins at 巳; 巳 becomes 子, and birth occurs after ten months. The male starts at 巳 and reaches 寅; the female starts at 巳 and reaches 申. Hence male years begin at 寅, female years at 申. All characters in this group follow 包.

entries.text: Effectively a variant form of 囱 as described in 窓 (compression), suggesting the compression of time in rushing → *busy*; *rushed*; *hurried*. Compare 趣.
凶# hole/cavity + 勹 wrap, here a shape indicator suggesting the chest → the cavity of the *breast*. *Nomadic race* (of the north in ancient China) is a borrowed meaning.
聲也。从勹凶聲。

translation.text: A sound. Formed from 勹, with 凶 indicating the sound.

entries.text: 勹 an abbreviated form# of 包 (envelop) + 米 rice → wrap the hands about a handful of rice → a *handful*.
在手曰匊。从勹、米。

translation.text: What is held in the hand is 匊. Formed from 勹 and 米.

entries.text: 勹 an abbreviated form# of 包 (encompass/envelop) + 缶 bulging earthenware jug/vase → knead clay in a vessel in creating *pottery*, *ceramics* or *porcelain*.
瓦器也。从缶，包省聲。古者昆吾作匋。案：《史篇》讀與缶同。

translation.text: An earthenware vessel. From 缶; abbreviated 包 supplies the sound. Anciently Kunwu made pottery. Note: the Scribe's Primer pronounces it the same as 缶.

entries.text: 帀也。从勹从合，合亦聲。

translation.text: To surround. Formed from 勹 and 合; 合 also indicates the sound.

entries.text: As per 甫# (spread) + 勹 wrap → lie on one's stomach (as though wrapping the earth with one's belly) → *crawl*. Compare 巴.
手行也。从勹甫聲。

translation.text: To move on the hands. Formed from 勹, with 甫 indicating the sound.

entries.text: 包# envelop + 夸 (U-shaped) → *gourd* (compare 瓢 and 瓠) → *container made from a gourd*; *musical instrument made from a gourd*.
瓠也。从包，从夸聲。包，取其可包藏物也。

translation.text: A bottle gourd. Formed from 包, with 夸 indicating the sound. 包 is used because it can contain things.

entries.text: As per 畐# as described in 副 (abundance) + 勹 wrap → large number of fighters crawling stealthily to surround an enemy (compare 偪 and 逼) → *fall prostrate*; *crawl*.
伏地也。从勹畐聲。

translation.text: To lie prostrate on the ground. Formed from 勹, with 畐 indicating the sound.

entries.text: A depiction of a spoon-like eating implement with double, aligned prongs → *spoon* → *dagger*. Note that many publications offer as the standard form of 匕 the way it appears, for example, in 牝, eliminating the leftward protrusion of the horizontal stroke.
相與比敘也。从反人。匕，亦所以用比取飯，一名柶。凡匕之屬皆从匕。

translation.text: To compare and arrange with one another. Formed from reversed 人. 匕 is also used to take food by close scooping; another name is 柶. All characters in this group follow 匕.

entries.text: The relevant bronzeware inscription form shows a fallen person aligned with a seated person. A seal inscription form has a standing person aligned with another person, the latter assuming a curious pose. The meanings *transformation*, *change*, *assume a disguise*, *bewitch* and *deceive* suggest that the two figures depicted in 化 are one and the same individual, who has undergone a transformation in posture or appearance.
教行也。从𠤎从人，𠤎亦聲。

translation.text: Teaching put into practice. Formed from 𠤎 and 人; 𠤎 also indicates the sound.

entries.text: The relevant oracle bone form of this character shows two figures, one with his back turned → turn one's back to the enemy and flee (along a winding course) → *flee* → *north* (← flee to the north; or, turn one's back to the cold north wind) → *go northward*.
𦮃也。从二人相背。凡北之屬皆从北。

translation.text: To turn one’s back. Formed from two people back to back. All characters in this group follow 北.

entries.text: 頭𩪦也。从匕；匕，相匕著也。巛象髮，囟象匘形。

translation.text: The brain or marrow of the head. Formed from 匕, representing close attachment; 巛 depicts hair, 囟 the shape of the brain.

entries.text: As per 是# (spoon) + 匕 double-pronged eating implement → *spoon*. 匙 was devised to replace 是 after 是 acquired its extended meanings.
匕也。从匕是聲。

translation.text: A spoon. Formed from 匕, with 是 indicating the sound.

entries.text: A depiction of a large *enclosure* → *shape indicator*. Conceptually, the character suggests the idea of spreading within a large enclosure. Distinguish 匚 from 匸.
受物之器。象形。凡匚之屬皆从匚。讀若方。

translation.text: A vessel for receiving things. A pictograph. All characters in this group are formed from 匚. Read like 方.

entries.text: 似羹魁，柄中有道，可以注水。从匚也聲。

translation.text: Like a soup ladle, with a channel in its handle for pouring water. Formed from 匚, with 也 indicating the sound.

entries.text: 斤 ax + 匚# enclosure → create a finely crafted enclosure → *craftsman*; *master*.
木工也。从匚从斤。斤，所以作器也。

translation.text: A woodworker. Formed from 匚 and 斤. 斤 is what is used to make utensils.

entries.text: As per 王# (extend) + 匚 enclosure/frame → extend within/over a container or framing object → *reform*; *correct* (← spread and conform to the contours of a containing/framing object) → *assist*; *save* (← aid in reforming/correcting).
飲器，筥也。从匚㞷聲。

translation.text: A drinking vessel; a basket. Formed from 匚, with 㞷 indicating the sound.

entries.text: As per 甲# (press down upon) + 匚 enclosure → (lidded) *box*. Compare 篋.
匱也。从匚甲聲。

translation.text: A chest. Formed from 匚, with 甲 indicating the sound.

entries.text: 藏也。从匚夾聲。

translation.text: To store. Formed from 匚, with 夾 indicating the sound.

entries.text: As per 非# (spread in alignment to right and left) + 匚 enclosure → basket with lids/doors that open in alignment to both sides. *Bandit*, *evil person* and *not* are borrowed meanings.
器，似竹筐。从匚非聲。《逸周書》曰：“實玄黃于匪。”

translation.text: A vessel resembling a bamboo basket. Formed from 匚, with 非 indicating the sound. The Lost Book of Zhou says: 'Place the black and yellow silk in the basket.'

entries.text: 古器也。从匚曶聲。

translation.text: An ancient vessel. Formed from 匚, with 曶 indicating the sound.

entries.text: 甌，器也。从匚俞聲。

translation.text: A bowl, a kind of vessel. Formed from 匚, with 俞 indicating the sound.

entries.text: 淮# is as per 隹 (exert downward pressure) + 水 water → heavy buildup of water → name of a particular river. 匯 adds 匸 (contain) → converging waters that collect in a containing basin → *confluence*; *swirling water*.
器也。从匚淮聲。

translation.text: A vessel. Formed from 匚, with 淮 indicating the sound.

匯.explanation: Converge, collect into one place, foreign exchange or remittance senses, not the summary/compilation sense 彙.
匯.usageCaveat: Choose using the word and meaning; not a universal replacement for 汇.
匯.evidenceScope: Unihan 17.0 forward relationship; lexical use and 2013 official classification not independently exhaustively checked.

彙.evidenceScope: OpenCC 1.4.2 explicitly maps 汇总→彙總.

sources.basis: Lexical example explicitly found in OpenCC 1.4.2 STPhrases

entries.text: 宗廟盛主器也。《周禮》曰：“祭祀共匰主。”从匚單聲。

translation.text: A vessel for holding the ancestral tablet in a temple. The Rites of Zhou says: 'For sacrifices, supply the tablet container and tablet.' Formed from 匚, with 單 indicating the sound.

entries.text: As per 貴# (valuable goods) + 匚 enclosure → empty a container of its valuables → *empty container*; *empty*; *lacking*.
匣也。从匚貴聲。

translation.text: A chest or box. Formed from 匚, with 貴 indicating the sound.

entries.text: As per 僉# (assemble) + 匚 enclosure → *box* containing an assemblage of items → *cosmetics/toiletries box*.
渌米籔也。从匚算聲。

translation.text: A basket for draining rice. Formed from 匚, with 算 indicating the sound.

entries.text: 匱也。从匚賣聲。

translation.text: A chest. Formed from 匚, with 賣 indicating the sound.

entries.text: A depiction of a long container (conceptually, beyond which objects stretch) → *contain*; *conceal*. Distinguish 匸 from 匚.
衺徯，有所俠藏也。从乚，上有一覆之。凡匸之屬皆从匸。讀與傒同。

translation.text: Slanting and enclosing, with something held hidden inside. Formed from 乚 with 一 covering it above. All characters in this group are formed from 匸. Pronounced the same as 傒.

entries.text: The relevant bronzeware inscription form is 厂 cliff/shape indicator (here suggesting a hanging piece of cloth) + two parallel vertical lines# → two pieces of cloth set out to dry and hanging side by side → *one* (of a pair) → *counter* (for animals).
四丈也。从八、匸。八揲一匹，八亦聲。

translation.text: Four zhang. Formed from 八 and 匸: eight folds make one 匹. 八 also indicates the sound.

entries.text: 盛弓弩矢器也。从匸从矢。《國語》曰：“兵不解医。”

translation.text: A container for bow and crossbow arrows. Formed from 匸 and 矢. The Discourses of the States says: 'The soldiers did not loosen their quivers.'

entries.text: An abbreviated form# of 晏 (settle) + 匸 contain/conceal → set an object in place, hiding it away → *hide*; *secrete*. *Bend* is a borrowed meaning.
匿也。从匸妟聲。

translation.text: To hide. Formed from 匸, with 妟 indicating the sound.

entries.text: As per 若# (supple) + 匸 contain/conceal → supple mulberry leaves hidden in a container → *hide*; *conceal*.
亡也。从匸若聲。讀如羊騶箠。

translation.text: To disappear or hide. Formed from 匸, with 若 indicating the sound. Read like 箠 in 羊騶箠; the reference is obscure.

entries.text: The relevant bronzeware inscription form shows a line that curves/bends in penetrating three enclosures → *division*; *sector* (← divide a narrow section into smaller parts).
踦區，藏匿也。从品在匸中。品，眾也。

translation.text: 踦區 means to conceal. Formed from 品 within 匸. 品 means a multitude.

entries.text: A depiction of objects pressed into a single unit in gathering → *ten* (← key unit in counting).
數之具也。一爲東西，|爲南北，則四方中央備矣。凡十之屬皆从十。

translation.text: The completeness of numbers. 一 represents east and west; | represents south and north, thus the four directions and center are complete. All characters in the 十 category are formed from 十.

entries.text: 疾飛也。从飛而羽不見。凡卂之屬皆从卂。

translation.text: To fly swiftly. Formed from 飛 with its feathers, 羽, unseen. All characters in this group are formed from 卂.

entries.text: The relevant oracle bone form of this character is 人person with a line drawn at the shin to indicate a person progressing in small increments through luxuriant vegetation (compare 年 and 延) → *one thousand* (← number reached by counting on and on). It is unclear whether it is 人 or the line element acting as the phonosemantic element.
十百也。从十从人。

translation.text: Ten hundreds. Formed from 十 and 人.

entries.text: Originally styled as 十# ten + 廿 twenty → *thirty*.
三十并也。古文省。凡卅之屬皆从卅。

translation.text: Three tens combined. An abbreviated ancient form. All characters in the 卅 category are formed from 卅.

entries.text: The relevant oracle bone form of this character shows a measuring scoop + a hand → raise a *measuring implement* to perform dry or liquid measurements → *measuring box*; *unit of measurement* (approximately 1.8 liters) → *box seat*.
十龠也。从斗，亦象形。

translation.text: Ten yue. Formed from 斗, also a pictograph.

entries.text: A depiction of a square-headed mallet, two or more of which would be used in alternation when pounding grain in the mortar framing the mallets. Latter half of a unit of measurement (e.g., for a group of twelve, 午 covers 7-12) as well as *11 A.M. to 1 P.M.* and *noon* are associated meanings in the sense of the alternating point of a given day. *Horse* (as the seventh sign of the Chinese zodiac) and *south* are borrowed meanings. In derivative characters such as 忤 and 許, 午 exerts the conceptual influence "yield," via the image of yielding so another person can carry out a task such as pounding grain.
啎也。五月，陰气午逆陽。冒地而出。此予矢同意。凡午之屬皆从午。

translation.text: To oppose. In the fifth month yin vital energy opposes yang and emerges through the earth. The same conception as 予 and 矢. All characters in this group are formed from 午.

entries.text: 艸之緫名也。从艸、屮。

translation.text: A general name for plants. Formed from 艸 and 屮.

entries.text: 牛 cow + 八# split right and left → split a cow in butchering it, the separate parts remaining in close proximity → *half* → *part(ly)*.
物中分也。从八从牛。牛爲物大，可以分也。凡半之屬皆从半。

translation.text: To divide a thing through the middle. Formed from 八 and 牛: cattle are large things that can be divided. All characters in the 半 category are formed from 半.

entries.text: The relevant seal inscription form shows a variant form of 左 (left hand) spread over the handle of an implement used to flatten or lower a surface, such as a spatula or a trowel → *low*; *lowly*; *base* (← bottom) → *vulgar*; *greedy*; *mean* → *humble*; *despise* (← make oneself/another lower).
賤也。執事也。从𠂇、甲。

translation.text: Lowly; one who performs service. Formed from 𠂇 and 甲.

entries.text: The relevant seal inscription form combines an abbreviated form# of 率 (compact unit) + 衣 clothing → uniform worn by soldiers compacted into an orderly unit → *common soldier* → *servant*. *Termination*, *finally*, *die* and *suddenly* are borrowed meanings. A variant form, 卆, appears in the Shinjitai (new character form) styles of 砕, 粋 and 酔.
隸人給事者衣爲卒。卒，衣有題識者。

translation.text: The clothing of serving bondservants is called 卒: clothing bearing identifying marks.

entries.text: As per 早# (rising of the sun) + a variant of 人 person → person who rises above others → *excel*. For the idea of being excellent in the sense of surpassing, compare 特. *Table* is a borrowed meaning.
高也。早匕爲㔬，匕卪爲卬，皆同義。

translation.text: High. 早 with 匕 makes 㔬; 匕 with 卪 makes 卬. They all have the same meaning.

entries.text: 劦 triples 力 power/energy → the combined, harmonious power of many persons, pressing on a central point from two or more sides. 協 is 劦# + 十 (gather) → the united energies of many → *unite*; *cooperation*.
眾之同和也。从劦从十。

translation.text: The common harmony of a multitude. Formed from 劦 and 十.

entries.text: The relevant oracle bone form of this character is a depiction of a hut or small storehouse. However, a seal inscription form is 屮 grass shoot + an element# combining 冂 boundary/enclosure and an inverted 入 pierced by two horizontal lines, suggesting sprouts placed inside a hothouse for cultivation → *south* (← direction associated with warmth, which hothouses were positioned to face).
艸木至南方，有枝任也。从𣎵𢆉聲。

translation.text: Plants reaching the south have branches capable of bearing growth. Formed from 𣎵, with 𢆉 indicating the sound; the wording 枝任 is uncertain.

entries.text: 卙卙，盛也。从十从甚。汝南名蠶盛曰卙。

translation.text: 卙卙: abundant. Formed from 十 and 甚. In Runan, abundance of silkworms is called 卙.

entries.text: 尃# combines 甫 (spread) + 寸 hand/action indicator → spread in announcing/proclaiming. 博 adds 十 (gather) → a collection of numerous objects, spread over a surface → *broad*; *expansive*; *extensive* → *gambling* (← spread out objects being gambled) → *hit the mark*.
大通也。从十从尃。尃，布也。

translation.text: Broadly comprehensive. Formed from 十 and 尃; 尃 means to spread.

entries.text: A depiction of cracks spreading over shells/bones burnt in a divination rite → *divination*; *fortune-telling*.
灼剥龜也，象灸龜之形。一曰象龜兆之從橫也。凡卜之屬皆从卜。

translation.text: To scorch and crack a tortoise shell. It depicts heating a tortoise shell. Another explanation: it depicts vertical and horizontal divination cracks. All characters in the 卜 category are formed from 卜.

蔔.explanation: 蔔 represents the radish-related use of 卜 (as in 蘿蔔); 卜 meaning divination remains 卜.
蔔.example: 萝卜 → 蘿蔔; 占卜 → 占卜
蔔.evidenceScope: Targeted review of individual relationships against 2013 通用规范汉字表 Appendix 1; not a comprehensive audit of every Unihan pair.

entries.text: A variant form of 弁 (cap; crown): *cloth crown*. *Restless* and *unsettled* are borrowed meanings; compare the phonetically close 翻 (flutter) and 奮 (bird flapping its wings → vigorous exertion).
卜以問疑也。从口、卜。讀與稽同。《書》云“卟疑”。

translation.text: To divine in order to resolve doubts. Formed from 口 and 卜. Pronounced the same as 稽. The Documents says: “卟 doubts.”

entries.text: An abbreviated form# of 貞 divination + 囗 circular enclosure (specific place) → use divination/*fortunetelling* to pick out, *fix upon* or *select* a site → *occupy* (← occupy a site that has been chosen) → (of a specific group, market or so on) *make up/account for*; *hold/command* (a share) (← be in possession ← occupy). Also, *state* and *tell* (← state the results of divination).
視兆問也。从卜从口。

translation.text: To inspect cracks and inquire. Formed from 卜 and 口.

entries.text: A depiction of a long-necked, rounded *jug* or container. Compare 由 and 酋.

entries.text: As per 圭# (jade object) + 卜 divination → jade object used in *divination* → *omen*.
筮也。从卜圭聲。

translation.text: To divine with stalks. Formed from 卜, with 圭 indicating the sound.

entries.text: A depiction of a *kneeling figure/person*. *Tally/check* is via a once-separate character that came to be written the same as 卩.
瑞信也。守國者用玉卪，守都鄙者用角卪，使山邦者用虎卪，士邦者用人卪，澤邦者用龍卪，門關者用符卪，貨賄用璽卪，道路用旌卪。象相合之形。凡卪之屬皆从卪。

translation.text: A credential of authority. State guardians use jade tallies; guardians of towns and border districts, horn tallies; envoys to mountain states, tiger tallies; those to 士邦 states, human tallies; those to marsh states, dragon tallies; gate and pass officials, matching tallies; trade, seal tallies; roads, banner tallies. Depicts matching halves. All characters in the 卪 group follow 卪. The category 士邦 is uncertain.

entries.text: The relevant seal inscription form is 人 person + 卩 here an abbreviated form# of 却 (withdraw in a kneeling position) → kneeling person looking up at a standing one → *look up at* → *high*.
Originally a depiction of a large *cup/goblet*. A variant form, 巵, appears in the derivative character 梔.
圜器也。一名觛。所以節飲食。象人，卪在其下也。《易》曰：“君子節飲食。”凡巵之屬皆从巵。

translation.text: A round vessel, also called 觛, for regulating eating and drinking. Depicts a person with 卪 below. The Changes says: “The gentleman regulates food and drink.” All characters in the 巵 group follow 巵.

entries.text: The relevant oracle bone form of this character is a depiction of a door or window with a bar aimed at preventing forced entry. A second oracle bone form omits the horizontal line to indicate that force has been exerted on the bar in bending and removing it → door or window the protective bar of which has been bent. The second form described came to be written 卯, and 卯 now conveys the sense of the first one as well. *Rabbit* (as the *fourth sign of the Chinese zodiac*), *east*, and *5-7 A.M.* are borrowed meanings. The modern ON pronunciations of most derivatives of 卯are the result of initial M- transforming to L- via the intermediary cluster ML-.
冒也。二月，萬物冒地而出。象開門之形。故二月爲天門。凡卯之屬皆从卯。

translation.text: To emerge or cover. In the second month all things push through the earth and emerge. It depicts an open gate; hence the second month is Heaven's Gate. All characters in this group are formed from 卯.

entries.text: The relevant seal inscription form is 爪 claw/hand + a variant of the abbreviated form# of 宛 (bending figures) seen in 怨 and 苑 → press down on a person in forcing him/her to kneel → *seal* (← make an impression by pressing down) → *print*; *impress*; *mark*; *sign*; *symbol*.
執政所持信也。从爪从卪。凡印之屬皆从印。

translation.text: The credential held by those exercising authority. Formed from 爪 and 卪. All characters in this group follow 印.

entries.text: The relevant bronzeware inscription form shows 厄# (withdraw in a kneeling position from a cliff) + a second crouching figure at top → kneel in a dangerous, slightly off-balanced position at a cliff → *danger*. Related meanings included *risky*; *critical* (condition); *close/narrow* (escape) → *nearly*; *almost*; *barely* (← close escape), as well as *fear* (for); *be anxious*; *uncertain*; *unreliable*; *dubious* and *doubt* (← fear/be anxious or doubtful about escaping a dangerous situation).
在高而懼也。从厃，自卪止之。凡危之屬皆从危。

translation.text: Being high up and afraid. Formed from 厃, stopping oneself with 卪. All characters in this group follow 危.

entries.text: 高也。从卪召聲。

translation.text: High. Formed from 卪, with 召 indicating the sound.

entries.text: The relevant bronzeware inscription form is 卩# (kneeling figure) immediately beside (or, depending on vantage point, opposite) a table piled high with food → *immediate* → *accession* (← draw into immediate proximity). *Namely* is a borrowed meaning.
去# withdraw + 卩 kneeling figure → *withdraw* in a kneeling position → *contrary*.
A depiction of a swarm of fish eggs → *egg*.
凡物無乳者卵生。象形。凡卵之屬皆从卵。

translation.text: All creatures without milk are born from eggs. A pictograph. All characters in this group are formed from 卵.

entries.text: 有大度也。从卪多聲。讀若侈。

translation.text: To have great breadth of mind. Formed from 卪, with 多 indicating the sound. Read like 侈.

entries.text: As per 𠔉# as described in 券 (wrap/roll up) + a bending figure → *curl*; *roll*; *roll up*; *reel*; *coil*; *wind* (up/around) → *volume* (of a set of *books*, originally, rolled *scrolls*).
厀曲也。从卪𢍏聲。

translation.text: The knee bent. Formed from 卪, with 𢍏 indicating the sound.

捲.explanation: 捲 is used when rolling, winding or curling; 卷 remains for a scroll, volume, paper or examination.
捲.example: 卷起 → 捲起; 试卷 → 試卷
捲.evidenceScope: Targeted review of individual relationships against 2013 通用规范汉字表 Appendix 1; not a comprehensive audit of every Unihan pair.

entries.text: Abbreviated form of 楚# whip (with the 疋 element written in variant form) + 卩 kneeling figure → whip a kneeling person, then dismiss him → *get rid of*; *remove* → *retire* (from office). Also, *unload* and *wholesale* (← get rid of).
舍車解馬也。从卪、止、午。讀若汝南人寫書之寫。

translation.text: To leave the carriage and unhitch the horses. Formed from 卪, 止 and 午. Read like 寫 in the Runan pronunciation of 寫書.

entries.text: 血 here an abbreviated form# of 恤 (commiserate) + 卩 kneeling figure (→ posture of an afflicted person) → *commiserate*/*comfort* another person.
憂也。从血卩聲。一曰鮮少也。

translation.text: To worry. From 血; 卩 supplies the sound. Another explanation: scarce or few.

entries.text: 節欲也。从卪谷聲。

translation.text: To restrain desire. Formed from 卪, with 谷 indicating the sound.

entries.text: 即食也。从皀卪聲。

translation.text: To approach food. From 皀; 卪 supplies the sound.

entries.text: The relevant bronzeware inscription form is 即 (kneel immediately beside a table piled high with food) + an element# showing an additional person on the other side of the table → two figures positioned on opposite sides of a table. 卿 was originally used with exclusive reference to elder members of families who were permitted to eat in front of an altar. However, over time it came to designate the rank of an aristocrat → *noble*; *lord*; *minister*; *head of a government agency*. *You* is via the use of the term by a ruler toward a subordinate.
脛頭卪也。从卪桼聲。

translation.text: The joint at the head of the shin. Formed from 卪, with 桼 indicating the sound.

entries.text: A depiction of a *cliff* concealing objects atop it (as observed from below; compare 厃 as described in 詹) → *shape indicator*.
山石之厓巖，人可居。象形。凡厂之屬皆从厂。

translation.text: A rocky mountain cliff where people can dwell. Pictographic. All characters in this group follow 厂.

entries.text: 仰也。从人在厂上。一曰屋梠也，秦謂之桷，齊謂之厃。

translation.text: To look upward. Formed from 人 above 厂. Another explanation: an eave timber, called 桷 in Qin and 厃 in Qi.

entries.text: An abbreviated form# of 却 (withdraw in a kneeling position) + 厂 cliff → withdraw in a kneeling position from a cliff → *be at a loss* (← be unable to progress) → *misfortune*; *disaster*.
科厄，木節也。从卪厂聲。賈侍中說，以爲厄，裹也。一曰厄，蓋也。

translation.text: 科厄, a knot in wood. Formed from 卪, with 厂 indicating the sound. Attendant Jia explains 厄 as wrapping. Another explanation: covering.

entries.text: As per 氐# (press) + 厂 cliff/shape indicator (here suggesting the outline of a *whetstone*) (← press on a whetstone; compare 砥).
柔石也。从厂氐聲。

translation.text: To smooth stone. Formed from 厂, with 氐 indicating the sound.

entries.text: As per 圭# (neat) + 厂 cliff/shape indicator → neatly carved *cliff* → *shore*.
山邊也。从厂圭聲。

translation.text: A mountain’s edge. Formed from 厂, with 圭 indicating the sound.

entries.text: As per 尨# (large) + 厂 cliff/shape indicator → *large* and *thick*, concealing object. *Be in a jumble* is a borrowed meaning.
石大也。从厂尨聲。

translation.text: A large stone. Formed from 厂, with 尨 indicating the sound.

entries.text: 唐厗，石也。从厂，屖省聲。

translation.text: 唐厗, a stone. Formed from 厂, with abbreviated 屖 indicating the sound.

entries.text: An abbreviated form of 釐 *small amount* → *unit of money*.

The relevant bronzeware inscription form is 高# high/tall (written upside down; compare 覃) + 厂 cliff/shape indicator → tall cliff → *thick*; *heavy* (← cliff composed of thick, heavy rocks) → *cordial*; *warm*(hearted) (← lay on kindness thickly).
山陵之厚也。从𣆪从厂。

translation.text: The thickness of mountains and hills. Formed from 𣆪 and 厂.

entries.text: 厜㕒，山顚也。从厂垂聲。

translation.text: 厜㕒, a mountain summit. Formed from 厂, with 垂 indicating the sound.

entries.text: As per 昔# (pile) + 厂 cliff/shape indicator → pile of shavings created in engraving → *place atop* (← place a knife atop an object being engraved); *polish* (← polish by placing one object atop another) → *whetstone*.
厲石也。从厂㫺聲。《詩》曰：“他山之石，可以爲𠪞。”

translation.text: A whetstone. Formed from 厂, with 㫺 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “Stones from other mountains can serve as whetstones.”

entries.text: 隱也。从厂非聲。

translation.text: Hidden. Formed from 厂, with 非 indicating the sound.

entries.text: 厂 cliff + an abbreviated form# of 泉 spring → round spring at the base of a cliff → *origin*. *Field* and *plain* are borrowed meanings.
治也。从厂秝聲。

translation.text: To put in order. Formed from 厂, with 秝 indicating the sound.

entries.text: The lower element# ( 屰 reverse + 欠 bent, open-mouthed figure) originally indicated a person vomiting, with ingested food reversing itself up the digestive tract. 厥 adds 厂 cliff/shape indicator (→ stiff body) → seizure accompanied by vomiting . *That* is a borrowed meaning. Note that in Chinese, the lower element acquired the associated meaning "hiccup," while 厥 was borrowed for use as a personal pronoun.
發石也。从厂欮聲。

translation.text: To set a stone in motion. Formed from 厂, with 欮 indicating the sound.

entries.text: 仄出泉也。从厂晷聲。讀若軌。

translation.text: A spring issuing sideways. Formed from 厂, with 晷 indicating the sound. Read like 軌.

entries.text: 猒# was originally 口 mouth + an obsolete element ( 肉 flesh and 犬 dog/beast) → the disagreeable sensation of rich/fatty meat pressing upon the intestines → *be satiated*; *become tired/sick of*. 厭 adds 厂, an accretion of uncertain function. For a cognate term in Old Chinese involving rich food, compare 甘.
笮也。从厂猒聲。一曰合也。

translation.text: To press down. Formed from 厂, with 猒 indicating the sound. Another explanation: to join.

entries.text: 厱諸，治玉石也。从厂僉聲。讀若藍。

translation.text: 厱諸, a stone used to work jade. Formed from 厂, with 僉 indicating the sound. Read like 藍.

entries.text: 厂 cliff/shape indicator + 萬 here an abbreviated form# of 邁 (pass over vigorously) → rough-surfaced whetstone used for vigorous polishing → *rough/tough*; *sharp*; *sharpen*.
旱石也。从厂，蠆省聲。

translation.text: A dry stone, 旱石; the recorded gloss is uncertain. Formed from 厂, with abbreviated 蠆 indicating the sound.

entries.text: As per 厭# (press upon) + 甲 (armor/helmet) → *shell* (← protective armor that presses upon the body of the creature occupying it) → *operculum* (botanical/zoological term for a lid/cover).
A depiction of a plow with neatly aligned prongs. Take *possession* of an object and *oneself* are borrowed meanings.
姦衺也。韓非曰：“蒼頡作字，自營爲厶。”凡厶之屬皆从厶。

translation.text: Wicked and crooked. Han Fei says: “When Cangjie made characters, acting for oneself was 厶.” All characters in this group follow 厶.

entries.text: 臂上也。从又，从古文。

translation.text: The upper arm. Formed from 又 and an ancient written form.

entries.text: The relevant oracle bone form of this character is 囗 circular enclosure + 大 stand outstretched. However, the phonetic evidence suggests that 大 was originally 屰# reverse, suggesting "reverse course and *withdraw* from a particular place" → *leave*; *go*; *pass* (away from); *disappear* → *last* (October etc.) (← past ← pass). Also, *resign* (a post) and *divorce* (← take leave of). Recall that although the modern forms are distinct, the earliest form of 屰 is 大 written in reverse.
人相違也。从大凵聲。凡去之屬皆从去。

translation.text: People separating from one another. From 大; 凵 supplies the sound. All graphs in this category contain 去.

entries.text: 絫坺土爲牆壁。象形。凡厽之屬皆从厽。

translation.text: To heap dug earth into walls. A pictograph. All characters in this group are formed from 厽.

entries.text: 專小謹也。从幺省；屮，財見也；屮亦聲。凡叀之屬皆从叀。

translation.text: Single-minded, minute and cautious. From abbreviated 幺; 屮 means just appearing, and also supplies the sound. All graphs in this category contain 叀.

entries.text: The relevant bronzeware inscription form combines 彡# (hair fully layered over the head) + a depiction of a young woman with three slender hairpins thrust deep into and commingling with her hair (compare 潛 and 妻) → *three* → *join*; *mix*; *meet* (← groups of three people commingling in coming, going or visiting ← three pins commingled in the hair) → *come*; *go*; *visit*; *obey*. As with 壱, 弐, and 拾, this character is used as a substitute for the usual number (in this case, 三) in documents as a precaution against forgery.
A depiction of a person's right arm contracted in surrounding or protecting an object resting on the shoulders → *above*; *beyond* → *again*; *moreover*; *or*.
手也。象形。三指者，手之𠛱多略不過三也。凡又之屬皆从又。

translation.text: A hand. A pictograph. It has three fingers because representations of the many divisions of a hand are abbreviated to no more than three. All characters in the 又 category are formed from 又.

entries.text: The relevant seal inscription form is an abbreviated form# of 爪 (pick/pluck) + an object → stab at an object with a forked implement to *catch* or *sandwich* it → *fork* (in the road); (Edo-era) *Y-shaped weapon for apprehending criminals*.
手指相錯也。从又，象叉之形。

translation.text: Fingers crossing one another. Formed from 又, depicting a forked form.

entries.text: The relevant oracle bone form of this character shows a person + a hand reaching toward another person (compare 服) → *reach/extend* and press a hand on the back of a fleeing person → *overtake* → *amount to*; *equal*. By further extension are *and* and *as well as* (← equally), while *come to*, *exert* (upon) and *affect* derive from the original sense of exerting pressure with one's hand.
逮也。从又从人。

translation.text: To reach. Formed from 又 and 人.

entries.text: The relevant oracle bone form of this character is 又# (right hand/arm) doubled → *work together* → *friend*; *companion* → *friendly*.
同𢖽爲友。从二又。相交友也。

translation.text: Those sharing the same intention are friends. Formed from two 又, expressing friendship with one another. [The source writes 𢖽 in the opening phrase.]

entries.text: The relevant oracle bone form of this character is 又 hand/action indicator + a thin sheet of wood → curve a thin piece of wood back upon itself → *bend back*; *return*; *warp*; *reverse*; *flutter*; *on the contrary*; *anti-* → *rebel*; *disobey*. *Counter for cloth or paddies/fields* is a borrowed meaning.
覆也。从又，厂反形。

translation.text: To turn over. Formed from 又, with 厂 in a reversed form.

entries.text: 日初出東方湯谷，所登榑桑，叒木也。象形。凡叒之屬皆从叒。

translation.text: When the sun first emerges from Tang Valley in the east, the 榑桑 on which it rises is the 叒 tree. Pictographic. All characters in this group follow 叒.

entries.text: 尗# shows a pendent, twisted bean vine (compare 弔, 弗, and 弟) + 小 small/slender → slender, hanging vine (compare also 寂). 叔 adds 又 hand/action indicator → pick beans from a slender, hanging vine → end → younger brother of one's father (← younger siblings on a figurative family vine ← beans on a vine; compare 弟 younger brother) → *uncle* (younger or older, either one).
拾也。从又尗聲。汝南名收芌爲叔。

translation.text: To gather. Formed from 又, with 尗 indicating the sound. In Runan, harvesting 芌 is called 叔.

entries.text: A depiction of pieces of material connected in a curved shape, suggesting reduction in size on account of being connected → *connect*.
綴聯也。象形。凡叕之屬皆从叕。

translation.text: To connect in succession. A pictograph. All characters in this group are formed from 叕.

entries.text: 耳 ear + 又# hand/action indicator → take hold of an enemy's severed head by one ear → *take*; *grasp*; *take away*; *seize*; *rob*; *remove*; *eliminate* → *obtain*; *get* (a prize/grade/salary etc.); *hand/pass along*; *pick up*; *come off/out*.
捕取也。从又从耳。《周禮》：“獲者取左耳。”《司馬法》曰：“載獻聝。”聝者，耳也。

translation.text: To capture and take. Formed from 又 and 耳. The Rites of Zhou says: “The captor takes the left ear.” The Methods of the Sima says: “Carry and present the 聝.” 聝 means an ear.

entries.text: The relevant oracle bone form of this character is 舟# (curved) boat (here a shape indicator suggesting a large, curved object) + an element combining 爪 claw/hand and 又 hand/action indicator → *receive/accept* a large, curved object → *receptacle*; *catch* (a ball); *popularity* (← receive general acceptance) → *reputation*; *be a success*. Also, *sustain* (damage) (← be on the receiving end of a damaging act) and *support(ing)* (← accept a supporting role), as well as *undergo* and *take an exam* (←be on the receiving end of a trying experience/exam) → *pass an exam*.
相付也。从𠬪，舟省聲。

translation.text: To hand to one another. From 𠬪; abbreviated 舟 supplies the sound.

entries.text: The relevant bronzeware inscription form is 二# align + an element combining 厂 cliff/shape indicator (here suggesting a hanging cloth or pelt) and a variant of 殳 action indicator → overlay the body with a garment → *conceal* (← body concealed by the garment overlaying it) → *false* (← conceal reality/the truth).
借也。闕。

translation.text: To borrow. The explanation is missing.

entries.text: As per 半# (split) + 反 bend back → split in rebellion → *revolt*; *rebel*.
半也。从半反聲。

translation.text: To split in half. Formed from 半, with 反 indicating the sound.

entries.text: 老也。从又从灾。闕。

translation.text: Old. Formed from 又 and 灾. The explanation is incomplete.

entries.text: The relevant seal inscription form is 又 hand/action indicator + an element# combining 宀 roof/building (here suggesting an enclosed space) and 火 fire → search a narrow aperture, using a torch/lamp. *Old man* and *elder* (n.) are borrowed meanings.
深明也。通也。从𣦼从目，从谷省。

translation.text: Deep understanding; penetration. From 𣦼, 目 and abbreviated 谷.

entries.text: As per 取# (take hold of) + 丵 as described in 對 (thick clump of tall grass) → take hold of and *gather bushes*/*shrubs* → *thicket*.
聚也。从丵取聲。

translation.text: To gather. Formed from 丵, with 取 indicating the sound.

entries.text: A depiction of a rounded cavity, and in particular the human *mouth* → *hole*; *entrance*. 口 can also function as a shape indicator.
人所以言食也。象形。凡口之屬皆从口。

translation.text: That by which people speak and eat. A pictograph. All characters in the 口 category are formed from 口.

entries.text: The relevant oracle bone form of 古 combines 口 mouth + an object filling it → expectorate *old*, *dried out*, *hard* food → *dry up*; *stale* → *used*; *old-fashioned*.
故也。从十、口。識前言者也。凡古之屬皆从古。

translation.text: Old or former. Formed from 十 and 口: remembering earlier words. All characters in the 古 category are formed from 古.

entries.text: Originally the same character as 局 (bending lines demarcating a frame). In 句, the sense of "demarcation" gave rise to the meanings *phrase*, *verse*, *line*, *clause* and *sentence*.
曲也。从口丩聲。凡句之屬皆从句。

translation.text: Curved. Formed from 口, with 丩 indicating the sound. All characters in the 句 category are formed from 句.

entries.text: As per 刀# (curve) + 口 mouth → *curl the lower lip* → *be appreciative*; *be ravenous for* (← appreciate/be ravenous for food; compare 饕) → *greedy*.

口# mouth + 卩 kneeling figure → kowtow in making a request → *prostrate* (← lower oneself) → *beat* (← beat another into a prostrate position) → *strike*. Note that the English term "kowtow" is via the compound 叩頭.
八 here an abbreviated form# of 余 (disperse) + 口 mouth → disperse breath from the mouth in speech. *Only* and *just* are borrowed meanings.
語巳詞也。从口，象气下引之形。凡只之屬皆从只。

translation.text: A particle ending an utterance. Formed from 口, depicting breath drawn downward. All characters in the 只 category are formed from 只.

entries.text: The relevant seal inscription form of 丩 shows it to be twisted threads. 叫 is 口 mouth +丩# for the sound alone to simulate a cry or calling noise (compare 号) → *yell*; *cry out*; *shout*; *scream* → *call*; *name* (in derogatory senses); *appeal* (for); *clamor*.
嘑也。从口丩聲。

translation.text: To call out. Formed from 口, with 丩 indicating the sound.

entries.text: As per 刀# (curve) + 口 mouth → curve the arm and beckon, supplementing oral summoning → *summon* → *term of respect*. From the idea of a person of superior rank beckoning to an inferior for service, the verb めす is used as a polite expression for the following senses: *eat*, *drink*, *put on*, *wear*, and *take* (a bath/a conveyance). めす is also used in the same way for *buy* or *catch* (a cold). *Invite* is a borrowed meaning.
𧦝也。从口刀聲。

translation.text: To call, 𧦝. Formed from 口, with 刀 indicating the sound.

entries.text: As per 八# (split right and left) + 口 mouth → exhale spurts of breath through both sides of the mouth. The compound 喇叭 refers to a trumpet.

The relevant oracle bone form of this character is a representation of a bent hook + 口 mouth → bend/cup a hand about the mouth to amplify the voice in shouting → shout/laugh/sing in a loud voice. *Possible* is an extended meaning (← make it possible to be heard at a distance), with *approve* by further extension (← approve of what has been made possible).
𦘫也。从口丂，丂亦聲。凡可之屬皆从可。

translation.text: The quality 𦘫, apparently agreeable or permissible. From 口 and 丂; 丂 also supplies the sound. All graphs in this category contain 可. [The rare cross-gloss is unresolved.]

entries.text: 囗 circular enclosure + 厶# (plow) → exert heavy downward pressure in plowing furrows into an enclosed field → *counter for machines* → *counter for cars*. 　In Japan, 台 was also adopted as a Shinjitai (new character form) to replace 臺, according to which 台 also bears the meanings *platform* and *pedestal*.
說也。从口㠯聲。

translation.text: Pleased. Formed from 口, with 㠯 indicating the sound.

entries.text: 訶也。从口七聲。

translation.text: To scold. Formed from 口, with 七 indicating the sound.

entries.text: The relevant oracle bone form of this character is 又 hand/action indicator + an upright tube for holding slender, inscribed bamboo slats → an official raising a slender tube containing bamboo slats inscribed with records → *chronicle*; *annals*; *history* (← contents of matters recorded). Also, *record keeper*. Originally the same character as 事, but 史 and 事 came to bear divergent meanings (compare the same process in 句 and 局).
記事者也。从又持中。中，正也。凡史之屬皆从史。

translation.text: One who records affairs. Formed from 又 holding 中; 中 means uprightness. All characters in the 史 category are formed from 史.

entries.text: The relevant seal inscription form is as per 又# (the right hand/arm) + an object → *right* hand/arm (used in protecting).
助也。从口从又。

translation.text: To assist. Formed from 口 and 又.

entries.text: 手口相助也。从又从口。

translation.text: Hand and mouth assisting one another. Formed from 又 and 口.

entries.text: 高气也。从口九聲。臨淮有叴猶縣。

translation.text: A lofty spirit or raised breath. Formed from 口, with 九 indicating the sound. Linhuai has Qiuyou county.

entries.text: 不可也。从反可。

translation.text: Not possible. From reversed 可.

entries.text: 口 mouth + 十# (gather) → voices gathered in harmonious supplication → *harmonize*. Also, *be realized/have one's prayer answered* (← grant a group's wish/request).

丂 is an object that extends before bending (compare 于). 号 is口 mouth + 丂# both for the idea of bending and for the sound to simulate a cry or calling noise produced by bending the throat → *call*; *name* → *number*; *indicator*. In Japan, 号 is a Shinjitai (new character form) replacing 號.
痛聲也。从口在丂上。凡号之屬皆从号。

translation.text: A sound of pain. From 口 above 丂. All graphs in this category contain 号.

entries.text: The relevant seal inscription form combines a variant of 人 person + 口# hole → peer through a narrow hole in overseeing or administrating → *administer*.
臣司事於外者。从反后。凡司之屬皆从司。

translation.text: A minister administering affairs outside. Formed from reversed 后. All characters in this group follow 司.

entries.text: 口 mouth (→ opening) + 入put in/enter → *straw bag*.
